```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---- Data load -----------------------------------------------------------
// typed:true would coerce countyfips ("08000") to a number and destroy the
// leading zero, so we load untyped and auto-type every column except that one.
raw = FileAttachment("output/netmig-comparison.csv").csv()
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
data = raw.map((d) => {
  const fips = d.countyfips;
  const t = d3.autoType(d);
  t.countyfips = fips;
  return t;
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// age_group is age at the END of the period (uniform 18-level grid, both
// periods share it). age_order 1..18 gives display order.
ageLevels = Array.from(new Set(data.map((d) => d.age_group)))
  .map((g) => ({ g, o: data.find((d) => d.age_group === g).age_order }))
  .sort((a, b) => a.o - b.o)
  .map((d) => d.g)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
countyOptions = {
  const others = Array.from(new Set(data.map((d) => d.county)))
    .filter((c) => c !== "Colorado")
    .sort();
  return ["Colorado", ...others];
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Chronological order drives every sort/legend/earliest-latest calc below.
periodOptions = ["1990-2000", "2000-2010", "2010-2020", "2020-2025"]
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
periodYears = {
  return {
    "1990-2000": { start: 1990, end: 2000 },
    "2000-2010": { start: 2000, end: 2010 },
    "2010-2020": { start: 2010, end: 2020 },
    "2020-2025": { start: 2020, end: 2025 }
  };
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Fixed period -> colour mapping so a period's colour never changes as the
// selection changes. Keeps SDO navy/orange for the two most-viewed periods.
periodColor = new Map([
  ["1990-2000", "#6B7280"],
  ["2000-2010", "#8B5FBF"],
  ["2010-2020", "#E3791C"],
  ["2020-2025", "#003E82"]
])
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Same swatch order Plot's "tableau10" scheme would assign, but held here as
// an explicit array so the SVG export can redraw the legend.
countyColors = d3.schemeTableau10
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
measureSlug = (key) => (key === "rate_per_1000" ? "rate" : "people")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---- SVG export ----------------------------------------------------------
// Observable Plot returns a bare <svg>, or (whenever a colour legend is
// requested inline) a <figure> wrapping an <svg> plus an HTML legend div.
// PowerPoint needs a self-contained, explicitly-sized SVG: Plot's on-page
// look depends on a stylesheet class (currentColor fills/strokes) that does
// not travel with a downloaded file, and the HTML legend has to be redrawn
// as SVG shapes/text since it isn't part of the <svg> at all.
buildExportSvg = (chart, legend) => {
  // Plot returns a bare <svg> for a plain chart, but a <figure> wrapping the
  // legend (tiny per-swatch <svg> icons!) plus the real chart <svg> whenever
  // a colour legend is requested inline -- querySelector("svg") would grab
  // the first swatch icon instead of the chart, so pick the largest one.
  const root =
    chart.tagName === "svg"
      ? chart
      : Array.from(chart.querySelectorAll("svg")).reduce((best, s) => {
          const area = (r) => r.width * r.height;
          if (!best) return s;
          return area(s.getBoundingClientRect()) > area(best.getBoundingClientRect()) ? s : best;
        }, null);
  if (!root) return null;
  const svg = root.cloneNode(true);

  // Inline every element's *computed* fill/stroke/font so nothing depends
  // on a CSS class that won't be present when the file is opened elsewhere.
  const origEls = root.querySelectorAll("*");
  const cloneEls = svg.querySelectorAll("*");
  origEls.forEach((o, i) => {
    const c = cloneEls[i];
    if (!c) return;
    const cs = getComputedStyle(o);
    if (cs.fill && cs.fill !== "none") c.setAttribute("fill", cs.fill);
    if (cs.stroke && cs.stroke !== "none" && cs.stroke !== "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)") {
      c.setAttribute("stroke", cs.stroke);
    }
    if (o.tagName === "text" || o.tagName === "tspan") {
      c.setAttribute("font-family", cs.fontFamily);
      c.setAttribute("font-size", cs.fontSize);
    }
  });

  const w = +(root.getAttribute("width") ?? root.clientWidth ?? 800);
  const h = +(root.getAttribute("height") ?? root.clientHeight ?? 400);
  svg.setAttribute("width", w);
  svg.setAttribute("height", h);
  svg.setAttribute("viewBox", root.getAttribute("viewBox") ?? `0 0 ${w} ${h}`);
  svg.setAttribute("xmlns", "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg");

  if (legend && legend.domain.length) {
    const itemW = 150;
    const rowH = 20;
    const perRow = Math.max(1, Math.floor(w / itemW));
    const rows = Math.ceil(legend.domain.length / perRow);
    const legendH = 10 + rows * rowH;
    svg.setAttribute("height", h + legendH);
    svg.setAttribute("viewBox", `0 0 ${w} ${h + legendH}`);
    const wrapper = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "g");
    wrapper.setAttribute("transform", `translate(0, ${legendH})`);
    while (svg.firstChild) wrapper.appendChild(svg.firstChild);
    svg.appendChild(wrapper);
    legend.domain.forEach((label, i) => {
      const col = i % perRow;
      const row = Math.floor(i / perRow);
      const x = 6 + col * itemW;
      const y = 6 + row * rowH;
      const rect = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "rect");
      rect.setAttribute("x", x);
      rect.setAttribute("y", y);
      rect.setAttribute("width", 11);
      rect.setAttribute("height", 11);
      rect.setAttribute("fill", legend.range[i % legend.range.length]);
      svg.appendChild(rect);
      const text = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "text");
      text.setAttribute("x", x + 15);
      text.setAttribute("y", y + 9.5);
      text.setAttribute("font-size", "11px");
      text.setAttribute("font-family", "Arial, sans-serif");
      text.setAttribute("fill", "#212529");
      text.textContent = label;
      svg.appendChild(text);
    });
  }

  return svg;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
downloadChartSvg = (chart, filename, legend = null) => {
  const svg = buildExportSvg(chart, legend);
  if (!svg) return;
  const xml = new XMLSerializer().serializeToString(svg);
  const blob = new Blob([xml], { type: "image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8" });
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  const a = document.createElement("a");
  a.href = url;
  a.download = filename;
  document.body.appendChild(a);
  a.click();
  a.remove();
  setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000);
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
svgDownloadButton = (chart, filename, legend = null) => {
  const btn = html`<button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary dl-button">⬇ Download SVG</button>`;
  btn.onclick = () => downloadChartSvg(chart, filename, legend);
  return btn;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// One place that defines both first-class measures. Every chart, KPI, and
// table column reads formatting/labels from here so switching the selector
// can never leave a stale label or number format behind.
measures = {
  const rate_per_1000 = {
    key: "rate_per_1000",
    label: "Annual net migration rate (per 1,000 people)",
    short: "Rate per 1,000",
    axis: "Net migration rate (annual, per 1,000)",
    fmt: (v) => (v < 0 ? "−" : "+") + d3.format(",.1f")(Math.abs(v)) + " per 1,000",
    fmtShort: (v) => (v < 0 ? "−" : "+") + d3.format(",.1f")(Math.abs(v)),
    tickFormat: (v) => d3.format("+,.0f")(v)
  };
  const netmig_annual = {
    key: "netmig_annual",
    label: "Annual net migration (people per year)",
    short: "People per year",
    axis: "Net migration (people per year)",
    fmt: (v) => (v < 0 ? "−" : "+") + d3.format(",.0f")(Math.abs(v)) + "/yr",
    fmtShort: (v) => (v < 0 ? "−" : "+") + d3.format(",.0f")(Math.abs(v)),
    tickFormat: (v) => d3.format("+,")(v)
  };
  return { rate_per_1000, netmig_annual };
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Reconstructs the cohort's starting age group from the grid spacing (both
// periods sit on the same 5-year grid, and years is always a multiple of 5),
// so the CSV doesn't need a redundant origin column.
originLabel = (age_order, years) => {
  const idx = age_order - years / 5;
  return idx < 1 ? "Born during period" : ageLevels[idx - 1];
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
cohortLabel = (d) => {
  const py = periodYears[d.period];
  const origin = originLabel(d.age_order, d.years);
  const originText = origin === "Born during period"
    ? "Born during the period"
    : `${origin} in ${py.start}`;
  return `${originText} → ${d.age_group} in ${py.end}`;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Aggregating rate_per_1000 by summing rows would be wrong (it's a ratio);
// the correct aggregate rate is total annual net migration over total mean
// population. This is used anywhere a KPI sums across age groups.
aggregateMeasure = (rows, measureKey) => {
  const annual = d3.sum(rows, (d) => d.netmig_annual);
  const pop = d3.sum(rows, (d) => d.mean_pop);
  return measureKey === "rate_per_1000" ? (pop > 0 ? (annual / pop) * 1000 : 0) : annual;
}
```

# Compare periods

## {.sidebar}

Follow one area across the selected periods to see how its age profile of
net migration shifted.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof area_p = Inputs.select(countyOptions, { label: "Area", value: "Colorado" })
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof periods_p = Inputs.checkbox(periodOptions, { label: "Periods", value: periodOptions })
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof sex_p = Inputs.radio(["Total", "Male", "Female"], { label: "Sex", value: "Total" })
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof measure_p = Inputs.radio(
  new Map([
    ["Rate per 1,000 (annual)", "rate_per_1000"],
    ["People per year (annual)", "netmig_annual"]
  ]),
  { label: "Measure", value: "rate_per_1000" }
)
```

<div class="control-hint">Rates let you compare areas of different sizes.</div>

::: {.callout-note}
Age groups are age at the **end** of the period. A bar labeled "25-29" in
2020-2025 follows the people who were 20-24 in 2020. Hover any mark to see
where that cohort started.
:::

::: {.hidden}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Chronological order regardless of the order the checkboxes report back in;
// fall back to every period if the user unchecks all of them.
selectedPeriods_p = {
  const sel = periodOptions.filter((p) => periods_p.includes(p));
  return sel.length ? sel : periodOptions;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
earliestPeriod_p = selectedPeriods_p[0]
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
latestPeriod_p = selectedPeriods_p[selectedPeriods_p.length - 1]
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
rows_p = data.filter(
  (d) => d.county === area_p && d.sex_label === sex_p && selectedPeriods_p.includes(d.period)
)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
byPeriod_p = d3.group(rows_p, (d) => d.period)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
valEarliest_p = aggregateMeasure(byPeriod_p.get(earliestPeriod_p) ?? [], measure_p)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
valLatest_p = aggregateMeasure(byPeriod_p.get(latestPeriod_p) ?? [], measure_p)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
peakRow_p = (byPeriod_p.get(latestPeriod_p) ?? [])
  .reduce((a, b) => (b[measure_p] > a[measure_p] ? b : a))
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Earliest vs. latest of the *selected* periods -- with only two selected
// this is exactly the old two-period comparison; with more it summarizes
// the full span while the grouped-bar chart above shows every period.
shiftRows_p = Array.from(
  d3.group(rows_p.filter((d) => d.period === earliestPeriod_p || d.period === latestPeriod_p), (d) => d.age_group),
  ([age_group, arr]) => {
    const r1 = arr.find((d) => d.period === earliestPeriod_p);
    const r2 = arr.find((d) => d.period === latestPeriod_p);
    return {
      age_group,
      age_order: r1.age_order,
      v1: r1[measure_p],
      v2: r2[measure_p],
      diff: r2[measure_p] - r1[measure_p]
    };
  }
).sort((a, b) => a.age_order - b.age_order)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
biggestShift_p = shiftRows_p.reduce((a, b) => (Math.abs(b.diff) > Math.abs(a.diff) ? b : a))
```

:::

```{ojs}
chart_p1 = Plot.plot({

  color: {
    domain: selectedPeriods_p,
    range: selectedPeriods_p.map((p) => periodColor.get(p)),
    legend: true,
    label: "Period"
  },
  marks: [
    Plot.ruleY([0]),
    Plot.barY(rows_p, {
      x: "period",
      y: measure_p,
      fx: "age_group",
      fill: "period",
      title: (d) => `${cohortLabel(d)}\n${measures[measure_p].fmt(d[measure_p])}`
    })
  ]
})
```

```{ojs}
  chart_p1,
  `co-netmig-compare-periods-${area_p.replace(/\s+/g, "_")}-${measureSlug(measure_p)}.svg`,
  { domain: selectedPeriods_p, range: selectedPeriods_p.map((p) => periodColor.get(p)) }
```

### Row {height="38%"}

::: {.card title="How each age group shifted" width="45%"}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
md`**${earliestPeriod_p} → ${latestPeriod_p}**${selectedPeriods_p.length > 2 ? " (earliest vs. latest of the selected periods)" : ""}`
```

```{ojs}
chart_p2 = Plot.plot({
  width,
  height: 340,
  marginLeft: 55,
  y: { domain: ageLevels, label: null },
  x: {
    label: `Change in ${measures[measure_p].short.toLowerCase()}`,
    tickFormat: measures[measure_p].tickFormat,
    grid: true
  },
  marks: [
    Plot.ruleX([0]),
    Plot.barX(shiftRows_p, {
      x: "diff",
      y: "age_group",
      fill: (d) => (d.diff >= 0 ? "#003E82" : "#E3791C"),
      title: (d) =>
        `${d.age_group}: ${measures[measure_p].fmtShort(d.v1)} → ${measures[measure_p].fmtShort(d.v2)} (Δ ${measures[measure_p].fmt(d.diff)})`
    })
  ]
})
```

Navy = the rate rose between periods; orange = it fell (or turned negative).

```{ojs}

)
```

```{ojs}
downloadLink_p = {
```

# Compare areas

## {.sidebar}

Pick one period and 2+ areas to compare their age profiles directly.
Colorado is always available as a statewide reference (shown dashed).

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof period_a = Inputs.select(periodOptions, { label: "Period", value: "2020-2025" })
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof counties_a = Inputs.select(countyOptions, {
  label: "Areas (ctrl/cmd-click for multiple)",
  multiple: 6,
  value: ["Colorado", "Denver", "Weld", "Boulder"]
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof sex_a = Inputs.radio(["Total", "Male", "Female"], { label: "Sex", value: "Total" })
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof measure_a = Inputs.radio(
  new Map([
    ["Rate per 1,000 (annual)", "rate_per_1000"],
    ["People per year (annual)", "netmig_annual"]
  ]),
  { label: "Measure", value: "rate_per_1000" }
)
```

<div class="control-hint">Rates let you compare areas of different sizes.</div>

::: {.callout-note}
Age groups are age at the **end** of the selected period.
:::

::: {.hidden}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
rows_a = data.filter(
  (d) => d.period === period_a && counties_a.includes(d.county) && d.sex_label === sex_a
)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
spreadByAge_a = Array.from(d3.group(rows_a, (d) => d.age_group), ([age_group, arr]) => ({
  age_group,
  age_order: arr[0].age_order,
  spread: d3.max(arr, (d) => d[measure_a]) - d3.min(arr, (d) => d[measure_a])
}))
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
widest_a = spreadByAge_a.length
  ? spreadByAge_a.reduce((a, b) => (b.spread > a.spread ? b : a))
  : { age_group: "n/a", spread: 0 }
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
statewideRef_a = data.find(
  (d) =>
    d.county === "Colorado" &&
    d.period === period_a &&
    d.sex_label === sex_a &&
    d.age_group === "25-29"
)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
downloadLink_a = {
  const csv = d3.csvFormat(tableRows_a);
  const blob = new Blob([csv], { type: "text/csv" });
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  return html`<a class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary dl-button" href="${url}" download="netmig_${period_a}_areas.csv">⬇ Download CSV</a>`;
}
```

:::

# Methods

## Row

::: {.card title="What this dashboard shows"}

This dashboard compares Colorado's implied net migration by age across
**64 counties** and **four periods** (1990-2000, 2000-2010, 2010-2020, and
2020-2025), estimated as a demographic residual: population change minus
births plus deaths, by age cohort. Full derivation, validation, and
county-by-county narrative are in the companion report:
[netmig-by-age.html](netmig-by-age.html).

### Reading the age groups

`age_group` is **age at the end of the period**, not the start. A bar or point
labeled `25-29` in the 2020-2025 period represents the cohort that was 20-24 in
2020 and turned 25-29 by 2025 -- follow the arrow in any tooltip
("20-24 in 2020 &rarr; 25-29 in 2025") to see where that group started. All
four periods share the same 18 age-group levels, which is what makes them
directly comparable group-for-group.

### Choosing a measure

Two measures are offered as equal, first-class options:

- **Annual net migration (people per year)** -- the period-level net migration
  divided by the period's length (10 or 5 years). This is a headcount and is
  affected by the size of the area.
- **Annual net migration rate (per 1,000 people)** -- the same annualized
  figure divided by the cohort's average population and multiplied by 1,000.
  This is the size-neutral measure: it is what lets a small county be compared
  fairly against Denver or the state as a whole. It is the default.

Both measures are annualized, so **both are valid to compare across all four
periods** even though three of them (1990-2000, 2000-2010, 2010-2020) are 10
years long and the most recent (2020-2025) is 5. (The raw, un-annualized
period-level net migration is not shown in this dashboard for exactly that
reason -- it is not comparable across periods of different length.)

### The headline pattern

The 25-29 age group traces Colorado's boom-bust migration history: an annual
rate of +38.4 per 1,000 in 1990-2000, roughly halving to +19.0 in 2000-2010,
recovering to +26.9 in 2010-2020, and then jumping to +36.3 in 2020-2025 --
this dashboard's sharpest, narrowest peak in the whole series. Older working
ages tell the opposite story: the 55-59 group ran positive in every prior
period (+8.96 in 1990-2000, +1.27 in 2000-2010, +1.26 in 2010-2020) and then
turned negative for the first time in 2020-2025 (-5.06). In short, Colorado
used to draw people at nearly every age -- the 1990s profile was positive
across almost the whole age range -- and now draws almost exclusively young
adults while older workers net out-migrate. Use the **Compare periods** tab
on Colorado with all four periods selected to see this shape change directly,
then switch the area selector to check whether your county of interest
follows the same pattern.

### Caveats

This recovers the migration implied by the Census Bureau's published county
age estimates, not an independent measurement -- see the companion report for
the full derivation, calibration checks, and caveats on group quarters and sex
detail. Small counties in particular can have age-specific rates moved
noticeably by a handful of records.

:::
